rationale: Re-registered the split-configuration execution after diagnosing the failed receipt 0517acf0c7cc4960ab2a9ea0eff68bf0 (exit 1, test failed, no evaluable observations): the run aborted in the earlier follower_in_live_cluster case, whose repair step called AddVoter after the live leader had already stepped down through its leader-lease check, so no split_configurations event was ever emitted and every comparison of that receipt is unknown. The harness now gives that earlier case a longer heartbeat, election and leader lease so a brief contact gap cannot unseat the live leader, waits boundedly for the leader before its repair step, and records that step's outcome instead of aborting the whole run. Local verification of the fixed harness: every case completes, the earlier case reports repaired true with no repair error, and the split case reproduces two leaders in the same term with disjoint quorums and no cross-side entry under the flag, against a single leader in the control.

experiment.revision_reason: Same split_configurations case and comparison set as the predecessor, with a harness fix in the earlier follower_in_live_cluster case so its leader-lease timing cannot abort the run before the split case executes: that case now uses a 300 ms heartbeat, election and leader lease, waits boundedly for the leader before its repair step and reports a repair error instead of failing the test.

scope.description: Whether a reconstruction-governed leader and the peers of the committed configuration can both lead and commit when a partition separates them. Twenty-one in-process cases: the nineteen previously exercised restart shapes plus a split_configurations case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-voter cluster is collapsed to one voter, snapshotted, made three voters again, the leader is disconnected from the other two in both directions and stopped, only it is restarted together with a fresh empty instance, and both sides are left to elect and commit.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the partition uses the transport's own Disconnect on both sides, and the fresh instance is connected only to the restarted leader.

The restarted leader's reconstruction is the single-voter configuration recorded by its own snapshot while the configuration entry in its log names three voters; the two partitioned peers keep the committed configuration.
Each side is given up to 800 ms to elect, then both are asked to commit one uniquely named entry with a 1500 ms timeout, and each side's log store is searched for the other side's entry afterwards.

The earlier cases in the same test now use a 300 ms heartbeat, election and leader lease where a live leader must survive a follower restart, and their repair step reports its outcome rather than aborting the run.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, healing of the partition, multiple sequential client changes, and any claim about what the cluster would do if the partition were repaired.

experiment.prefix: The split case builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), demotes both non-leader peers, applies 100 commands, takes leader.Snapshot(), promotes both peers back, applies ten more entries and emits a split_inputs CA_EVENT with the last configuration entry. It disconnects the leader from both peers in both directions, stops the leader, restarts it over its own stores with the case flag, starts one fresh empty instance connected only to it, and waits for it to lead; it then issues AddVoter for the fresh instance, waits for a leader among the two partitioned peers, records both sides' terms and reconstructed voter counts, has both sides commit a uniquely named entry with a 1500 ms timeout, waits, searches each side's store for the other side's entry, and emits a split_result CA_EVENT with both sides' leadership, terms, voter counts, commit outcomes, own and cross entry presence, the derived cross_entries_seen and whether both sides lead in the same term.
experiment.responsibility: Election quorums and leader commitments are computed from each node's own reconstructed configuration, so whether two quorums overlap is decided by that configuration rather than by the committed one.

comparisons.description: Partition case with the flag enabled: a cluster is not expected to have a leader on the restarted side and a leader among the peers of the committed configuration at the same time.
Partition case with the flag enabled: two leaders are not expected to hold the same term.
Partition case with the flag enabled: an entry committed on one side is expected to be visible to the other side's store, so both committed entries should be found across the two sides.
Control: with the flag disabled the restarted side cannot lead with only one of the committed configuration's three voters reachable, so only the other side leads.
